neighbours.label: something being unseen: 'invisible', 'hidden', 'can't see', as against things being visible or perceived by another sense
fire: Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it is completely invisible and has no smell.
The real damage from the leak was hidden behind the kitchen wall.
Most of an iceberg lies under the water where sailors can't see it.
Fine dust in the air is often invisible until the sun shines through it.
Burnout at work tends to stay invisible to managers until it is too late.
The old map revealed a hidden passage beneath the castle.
Radio waves pass through the room all day, though we cannot see them.
Many costs of the new road are invisible to the drivers who use it.
quiet: Carbon monoxide alarms are cheap and easy to fit in any kitchen.
The real damage from the leak was obvious as soon as we opened the door.
Most of an iceberg is made of fresh water from old snow.
Fine dust in the air is clearly visible when the sun shines through it.
Burnout at work tends to be discussed at the yearly staff meeting.
The old map showed a narrow road beneath the castle.
Radio waves pass through the room all day, and we can hear the music.
Many costs of the new road are listed on the council website.

predictions: fire 0.4-1.0 on invisible/hidden/can't see; 'visible', 'audible' and plain description below 0.16
